evidence: Measured in 4 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.05–0.15% of total volatiles (0.01–0.03mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Sesquithujene is a volatile sesquiterpene, a type of aromatic molecule that plants release into the air. In nature, it acts as a chemical signal that can attract or repel insects, playing a role in the complex communication between trees and the ecosystems around them.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified in the bark of ash trees and the flowers of the tropical plant Lantana camara.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to sesquithujene for its potential in ecological management and insect control. Early animal studies (Oxford level 5) are exploring how this volatile compound acts as a pheromone or host-based lure for the emerald ash borer, a destructive beetle. If this bears out, it could lead to highly targeted, natural trapping systems to protect vulnerable forests.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is animal research (Oxford level 5) focusing on insect behavior, with the remainder consisting of chemical and structural analyses.
